mainTopic: Taking wood from a סוכה on יום טוב: the משנה's rule, רבי שמעון's view, and why a condition cannot free the wood of a סוכה built for the חג, which stays holy for all seven days.
overview: The משנה rules that on יום טוב you may not take wood from a סוכה, only from wood near it. The גמרא asks why taking the nearby wood is not also taking apart a tent, and שמואל and רב מנשיא each define 'near' so that it is not part of the structure. A ברייתא then shows that רבי שמעון permits taking wood even from the סוכה itself. רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that רבי שמעון means a סוכה that already fell and was shaky, so nothing is taken apart and the owner had its wood in mind before יום טוב. The ברייתא also says everyone forbids the wood of a סוכה built for the חג, unless the owner made a condition. The גמרא asks how a condition can work, since a פסוק makes the סוכה holy 'to ה׳' for all seven days. רב מנשיא בריה דרבא answers that the condition only works for an ordinary hut, and אביי and רבא explain that a condition on decorations works only by stopping holiness from ever starting. Finally, the גמרא explains that unlike the אתרוג, whose מצוה stops each night, the סוכה's seven days count as one long day.

steps.title: The משנה: Not from the סוכה, only from beside it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on יום טוב one may not take wood from a סוכה, but one may take wood from what is near it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We do not take wood from a סוכה, only from what is near it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a rule: on יום טוב you cannot pull wood off a סוכה to use, but you may take wood that is near the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling wood off the סוכה itself would be taking apart a structure. Wood that is only near it is treated differently. The משנה does not explain what 'near' means, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
We do not take wood from the sukkah,
but only from what is near it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב you may not take wood from a סוכה, but you may take wood that is near it.

steps.title: Why is wood from near the sukkah any different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the problem with the סוכה is taking apart a tent, taking wood near it should be the same problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why is taking from the סוכה forbidden? Because it takes apart a tent. Then taking from near it also takes apart a tent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If taking from the סוכה is forbidden because it is סותר אהל (taking apart a tent), why is taking from 'near it' allowed?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the 'nearby' wood is also part of the structure in some way. If so, removing it would also break down the tent. The question pushes us to define what 'near it' really means.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
Why is it different from the sukkah, that one may not?
Because he takes apart a tent.
From what is near it too,
he takes apart a tent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the logic of the משנה's distinction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's permission to take wood from 'near' the סוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason for the ban is סותר אהל, and that same reason seems to apply to the nearby wood too.

steps.title: שמואל: 'Near' means leaning by the walls
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that 'near it' means wood leaning beside the walls, which is not part of the סוכה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: What does 'near' mean? Near the walls.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, answers the question. The 'nearby' wood is wood resting next to the walls, not part of the סוכה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wood leaning by the walls is not part of the walls or the roof. So taking it does not take apart any tent. The question in step 2 assumed 'near' wood was part of the structure, and שמואל says it is not.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
What is 'near'?
Near the walls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by defining 'near'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: 'near' means wood beside the walls.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the 'nearby' wood was part of the tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: The nearby wood only rests by the walls, so taking it does not take apart any tent.

steps.title: רב מנשיא: Even on the roof, if still tied in bundles
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא gives another answer: even wood lying on the roof is allowed if it is still in tied bundles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא said: You can even say it is talking about wood not near the walls. When that ruling was taught, it was about bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא offers a different answer to the question in step 2. Even if the 'nearby' wood lies on top of the סוכה and not by the walls, it can be taken if it is still tied up in bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tied bundles lying on the סוכה were never opened up to become part of the roof. So removing them is not taking apart the tent. This is a second way to explain the משנה, different from שמואל's.

phrases.english: Rav Menashya said:
You can even say it is where it is not near the walls,
when that was taught,
phrases.notes: 'That' points back to the ruling that allows taking wood 'from near it.'

phrases.english: it was about tied bundles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to step 2's question, different from שמואל's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative case definition: bundles not yet part of the roof.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wood on the roof would always count as part of the tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: Tied bundles are not part of the roof, so removing them is not סותר אהל.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי שמעון permits
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף teaches a ברייתא that repeats the משנה's rule and adds that רבי שמעון permits taking wood even from the סוכה itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף taught before רבי יוחנן: We do not take wood from the סוכה, only from what is near it. And רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more information. It shows that the משנה's rule is only one opinion, because רבי שמעון disagrees and allows taking wood from the סוכה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part matches our משנה word for word. The new part is that רבי שמעון permits. So our משנה follows the view that disagrees with רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Before him, in front of him

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef taught
before Rabbi Yochanan:
We do not take wood from the sukkah
but only from what is near it,
and Rabbi Shimon permits.
phrases.notes: He permits taking wood even from the סוכה itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that expands on the משנה and shows a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא forbids taking wood from the סוכה. רבי שמעון permits it.

steps.title: All agree about a סוכה built for the חג, unless he made a condition
steps.stepSummary: Everyone, even רבי שמעון, agrees that taking wood from a סוכה built for סוכות is forbidden during the חג. If the owner made a condition in advance, his condition decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that a סוכה made for the חג is forbidden during the חג. And if he made a condition about it, everything follows his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It sets a limit on רבי שמעון's permission: a סוכה built for the חג may not have its wood taken during the חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's permission covers an ordinary סוכה. A סוכה built for the חג of סוכות is different, and everyone forbids taking from it during the חג. But if the owner made a condition before the חג allowing it, we follow that condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A סוכה built for the festival of סוכות

steps.whatToRemember: Ordinary סוכה: the תנא קמא forbids and רבי שמעון permits. A סוכה built for the חג is forbidden during the חג according to everyone, unless the owner made a condition beforehand.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Agree' here includes רבי שמעון. Even he forbids taking wood from a סוכה built for the חג during the חג.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a condition made in advance can change the status of a סוכה built for the חג.

phrases.english: And they agree about a festival sukkah during the festival
that it is forbidden.
And if he made a condition about it,
everything follows his condition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא by limiting רבי שמעון's permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סוכה built for the חג is forbidden during the חג according to everyone, but a condition made in advance is followed.

steps.title: How can רבי שמעון allow taking apart a tent?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's ruling, because taking wood from the סוכה itself should be the forbidden act of taking apart a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי שמעון really permit this? But the person is taking apart a tent!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised that רבי שמעון permits taking wood from the סוכה itself. Pulling wood out of a standing סוכה looks like taking apart a tent, which is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem here is not מוקצה. It is the forbidden act of סותר אוהל, taking apart a structure. Even someone lenient about מוקצה should not allow that.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Shimon permit this?
phrases.notes: This refers to the ברייתא from step 5, where רבי שמעון allows taking wood even from the סוכה itself.

phrases.english: But he is taking apart a tent!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר? וְהָא קָא סָתַר אֻהְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמעון's lenient ruling quoted in the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's ruling that one may take wood from the סוכה itself
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking wood from a standing סוכה is סותר אוהל, a forbidden act no matter what one holds about מוקצה.

steps.title: The case is a סוכה that already fell
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says רבי שמעון is speaking about a fallen סוכה. There is no tent left to take apart, and רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Here we are dealing with a סוכה that fell. רבי שמעון follows his usual reasoning, because he does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the סוכה has already collapsed. Taking its wood is not taking apart a tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the סוכה has fallen, the problem of סותר אוהל is gone. The only remaining question is whether the wood is מוקצה. רבי שמעון is consistent with his general view that there is no מוקצה here.

keyTerms.meaning: Something set aside and not available for use on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Here we are dealing with a sukka that fell,
and Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning,
for he does not hold of muktze.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הָכָא בְּסוּכָּה נוֹפֶלֶת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by narrowing the case to a fallen סוכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון seemed to allow taking wood from a standing סוכה, which would be taking apart a tent.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only allows it from a סוכה that already fell, where the only issue is מוקצה, and he does not hold of מוקצה.

steps.title: Proof: רבי שמעון permits leftover lamp oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה. He permits oil left over in a lamp after it goes out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: The oil left over in a lamp or in a bowl is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה. The source is the case of oil left in a lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion forbids the leftover oil because it was set aside for burning. רבי שמעון permits it, which shows his lenient approach to מוקצה. The same reasoning would allow wood from a fallen סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: The leftover oil in the lamp
phrases.notes: This is oil left after a lamp, lit before שבת, goes out on שבת.

phrases.english: and in the bowl is forbidden.
And Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 8's claim that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about leftover oil in a lamp, which רבי שמעון permits

steps.title: A lamp is expected to go out, a סוכה is not expected to fall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. A person expects his lamp to go out, but he does not expect his סוכה to collapse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it comparable? There, a person sits and waits for when his lamp will go out. Here, does a person sit and wait for when his סוכה will fall?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא argues that the lamp case does not prove anything about the fallen סוכה. The two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the lamp, the owner knows from the start that it will go out and leave oil. In his mind, the oil was never fully set aside. With a סוכה, no one plans on it falling, so the wood may be set aside, even for רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, a person sits and waits
for when his lamp will go out;
here, does a person sit and wait
for when his sukka will fall?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם אָדָם יוֹשֵׁב וּמְצַפֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 9 as not matching the fallen סוכה case of step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the lamp oil and the fallen סוכה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The lamp's going out is expected, so the oil is not fully set aside. A סוכה's falling is unexpected, so its wood may be fully set aside.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון's leniency about מוקצה does not cover everything. It works where the owner expected to use the item. That is why the גמרא asks whether the owner expected the סוכה to fall.

steps.title: The case is a shaky סוכה
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the case is a shaky סוכה. Since before יום טוב, the owner had in mind that it might fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Here we are dealing with a shaky סוכה, so from yesterday his mind was on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק fixes the problem from step 10. The סוכה was shaky, so the owner already expected it might fall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the סוכה was weak, the owner thought from the day before that it could collapse. He never fully pushed its wood out of his mind. Now it matches the lamp case, and רבי שמעון's leniency applies.

keyTerms.meaning: From yesterday, the day before יום טוב

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, wood from a סוכה may be taken on יום טוב only if two things are true. The סוכה already fell, so nothing is taken apart, and it was shaky, so the owner expected it might fall and the wood is not מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Here we are dealing with a shaky sukka,
so that from yesterday his mind was on it.
phrases.notes: He means the owner already thought before יום טוב that the סוכה might fall and he could use its wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: הָכָא בְּסוּכָּה רְעוּעָה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection of step 10 by narrowing the case further to a shaky סוכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A סוכה is not expected to fall, so its wood should be מוקצה even for רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzMaskana: A shaky סוכה is expected to possibly fall, so the owner had its wood in mind from before יום טוב, just like the lamp oil.

steps.title: Can a condition work on a סוכה built for the חג?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's rule again: a סוכה built for the חג is forbidden, but a condition decides. Then it asks whether a condition can really work there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone agrees that a סוכה built for the חג is forbidden during the חג, and if he made a condition on it, everything follows his condition. But does a condition really work for it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the last line of the ברייתא and questions it. It asks whether making a condition can really allow using the wood of a סוכת החג. The next step gives the source behind this question, and step 14 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a condition made in advance lets the owner use the wood. The גמרא doubts this, because a סוכה built for the מצוה might be set aside in a way that no private condition can undo. The line is repeated here for this new question.

keyTerms.meaning: A סוכה built for the festival of סוכות

phrases.english: And all agree about a sukka of the festival during the festival
phrases.notes: This is the same line from the ברייתא in step 6, quoted again so the גמרא can question it.

phrases.english: that it is forbidden,
and if he made a condition on it,
everything follows his condition.
But does a condition work for it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's ruling from step 6 and opens a new challenge about it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that a condition decides for a סוכת החג
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A סוכה built for the מצוה may be set aside so strongly that a condition should not be able to release its wood.

steps.title: The wood of a סוכה is holy for all seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its challenge. רב ששת teaches that the wood of a סוכה is forbidden for all seven days, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא explains that the סוכה is holy 'to ה׳', just like the קרבן חגיגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב ששת say, in the name of רבי עקיבא, that we learn the wood of a סוכה is forbidden all seven days from the פסוק 'the festival of סוכות, seven days, to ה׳'? And a ברייתא explains: just as the קרבן חגיגה belongs to Heaven, so too the סוכה belongs to Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is giving the reason behind its question from step 12. It shows that the סוכה's wood is holy, so a condition should not be able to free it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that if a person makes a condition, he may use the סוכה. But the פסוק compares the סוכה to a קרבן, and you cannot make a condition to use a קרבן for yourself. So how can a condition work on the סוכה?

keyTerms.meaning: All seven days of the festival
Heaven's name: something becomes dedicated to ה׳
The festival peace-offering brought on the חג

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the source behind the question that began in step 12: how can a condition work if the סוכה is holy?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Sheshet say in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
From where do we know that the wood of a sukkah
is forbidden all seven days?
As it says: "The festival of Sukkot, seven days, to ה׳."

phrases.aramaic: וְתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁכְּשֵׁם שֶׁחָל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל הַחֲגִיגָה,
phrases.english: From where do we know that just as Heaven's name takes effect on the festival offering,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ חָל שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל הַסּוּכָּה
phrases.english: so too Heaven's name takes effect on the sukkah?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״חַג הַסּוּכּוֹת שִׁבְעַת יָמִים לַה׳״,
phrases.english: The verse teaches: "The festival of Sukkot, seven days, to ה׳."
Just as the festival offering is to ה׳,
phrases.notes: Here the word חַג means the חגיגה offering brought on the festival.

phrases.english: so too the sukkah is to ה׳.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that makes the question in step 12 sharp.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement that a condition works for a סוכה built for the חג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סוכה is compared to a קרבן, and holiness from a פסוק cannot be undone by a private condition.

steps.title: The condition applies only to an ordinary hut
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בריה דרבא answers that the end of the ברייתא, which allows a condition, is talking about an ordinary year-round hut. For a מצוה סוכה, a condition does not help.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא, the son of רבא, said: the end of the ברייתא is talking about a regular hut. But for a מצוה סוכה, a condition does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנשיא answers the question by splitting the ברייתא into two cases. The first part is about a מצוה סוכה, and the last part is about a regular hut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a סוכה used for the מצוה gets the holiness of 'to ה׳'. A regular hut was never holy, so a condition can let him use it. This keeps the ברייתא in line with רב ששת.

keyTerms.meaning: The last part of a משנה or ברייתא
An ordinary hut, not made for the מצוה
A סוכה made for the מצוה of the חג

phrases.english: Rav Menashya, son of Rava, said:
In the last part, we have come to an ordinary sukkah,
but a sukkah of מצוה,
a condition does not work for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְסוּכָּה דְעָלְמָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the ברייתא: the first part and the last part are about different kinds of סוכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the whole ברייתא, including the condition, was about a מצוה סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition only works for an ordinary hut. A מצוה סוכה cannot be freed by a condition.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows a condition works on סוכה decorations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב מנשיא. A ברייתא says that decorations hung in a properly made סוכה are forbidden until the end of the חג, but if he made a condition, it all goes by his condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't a condition work for a מצוה סוכה? But a ברייתא teaches: if he covered the סוכה properly and decorated it with cloths, hung fruits, wines, oils, flour, and wreaths of grain, he may not use them until the end of the חג. But if he made a condition, everything goes by his condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב מנשיא's answer. It brings a ברייתא where a condition clearly works even in a real מצוה סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'he covered it properly' show this is a kosher מצוה סוכה. Still, the ברייתא says a condition works for its decorations. That seems to contradict רב מנשיא's claim that a condition never works for a מצוה סוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: He covered it with סכך properly, so it is a kosher מצוה סוכה
To make use of, to take benefit from

phrases.english: And for a מצוה sukkah it doesn't work?
But it was taught: If he covered it properly
and decorated it with embroidered cloths
and with patterned sheets,
and hung in it nuts, almonds,
peaches, pomegranates, and clusters of grapes,
wines, oils, fine flour, and wreaths of grain stalks,
it is forbidden to use them

phrases.aramaic: עַד מוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג.
phrases.english: until the end of the last festival day of the holiday.
But if he made a condition about them,
everything follows his condition.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב מנשיא's rule that a condition never works for a מצוה סוכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about a properly made מצוה סוכה says a condition does work for its decorations.

steps.title: Decorations can be freed, but the סוכה wood cannot
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא explain that the condition works only when he says ahead of time that he is not separating himself from the decorations during בין השמשות, so holiness never takes hold of them. The wood of the סוכה becomes holy no matter what, so it is set aside for all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: the case is where he says, 'I am not separating myself from them all through בין השמשות,' so holiness never takes effect on them. But the wood of the סוכה, which does become holy, is set aside for all seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what kind of condition the decorations ברייתא means. It then shows why that condition cannot work on the סוכה's wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The condition on decorations does not undo holiness. It stops holiness from ever starting, because at the moment the חג begins he keeps his hold on them. The wood, though, is the סוכה itself, and holiness takes hold of it anyway, so it is מוקצה for all seven days. This keeps רב מנשיא's rule in place.

keyTerms.meaning: I am not separating myself from them; I keep my right to use them
Twilight, the moment when the חג begins
Became מוקצה, set aside from use

steps.whatToRemember: A condition can stop holiness from starting on סוכה decorations, if he says he is not separating himself from them at בין השמשות. The actual wood of a מצוה סוכה becomes holy no matter what, and it is set aside for all seven days.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the difference between the סוכה itself, whose holiness comes from the פסוק, and its decorations, where a person's intention can decide whether holiness ever begins.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava, who both say:
It is where he says: I am not separating myself from them
all through twilight,
so holiness does not take effect on them.
But the wood of the sukkah,
on which holiness does take effect,
is set aside for all seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 and supports step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Making the case narrower: the condition on decorations is a special kind that stops holiness from ever starting.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the decorations ברייתא proved that a condition can free anything in a מצוה סוכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Decorations can be kept free with a condition made before בין השמשות. The wood of a מצוה סוכה becomes holy anyway and is מוקצה for all seven days.

steps.title: Comparing the סוכה to seven אתרוגים set aside for seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the סוכה is different from a case of seven אתרוגים, where each אתרוג may be eaten right away (רב) or the next day (רב אסי), and is not held for all seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about this compared with what was taught: If someone set aside seven אתרוגים, one for each of the seven days, רב said he uses each one for the מצוה and may eat it right away. רב אסי said he uses each one and may eat it the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rule that the סוכה wood is holy for all seven days. It points to a case of אתרוגים, where the holiness does not last the whole חג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and רב אסי argue about when the אתרוג may be eaten: right after the מצוה, or the next day. But both agree that an אתרוג set aside for one day is not held for the whole חג. So why should the סוכה wood be held for all seven days?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? A way of asking why two cases are treated differently
אתרוגים, the citrus fruits used for the מצוה on סוכות

steps.confusionAlert: Don't get caught up in the argument between רב and רב אסי. The question uses what they agree on: neither one says the אתרוג stays holy for all seven days.

phrases.english: And what is different from that which was taught:
If someone set aside seven etrogim
for the seven days,
phrases.notes: He means one אתרוג for each day of the חג.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב: כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת יוֹצֵא בָּהּ
phrases.english: Rav said: With each and every one he fulfills the מצוה
and he may eat it right away.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב אַסִּי אָמַר: כׇּל אַחַת יוֹצֵא בָּהּ
phrases.english: And Rav Asi said: With each one he fulfills the מצוה
and he may eat it the next day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of Step 16 that the סוכה wood is holy for all seven days no matter what.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the wood of a סוכה is set aside for all seven days of the חג.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אתרוג set aside for the מצוה is only held for one day at most, even though it is also a מצוה item of the חג. So the סוכה should also not be held for the whole חג.

steps.title: אתרוג is a separate מצוה each day; סוכה is one long day
steps.stepSummary: The מצוה of אתרוג does not apply at night, so each day is its own מצוה. The מצוה of סוכה goes on day and night, so all seven days count as one long day.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the nights split up the days, so each day is its own separate מצוה. Here, the nights do not split up the days, so all the days are like one long day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing how the אתרוג and the סוכה are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only take an אתרוג by day, so every night breaks the מצוה, and each day starts fresh. You sit in a סוכה at night too, so the מצוה never stops for seven days. That is why the סוכה wood is held for the whole חג.

keyTerms.meaning: The nights split up the days
There / here; used to set two cases side by side

steps.whatToRemember: The סוכה wood is held for all seven days because the מצוה of סוכה never stops, not even at night. The אתרוג is only for the day, so each day is a new מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This idea of 'one long day' explains why the holiness of the סוכה wood lasts until the end of the חג, finishing the defense of רב ששת's rule.

phrases.english: There, where the nights split up the days —
phrases.notes: 'There' is the אתרוג, which you only take during the day.

phrases.english: each and every day
is a separate מצוה on its own.
Here, where the nights do not split up the days —
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the סוכה, where you sit at night too.

phrases.english: all the days are like one
long day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17 by showing a difference between אתרוג and סוכה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since an אתרוג is only held for one day, the סוכה wood should also not be held for all seven days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אתרוג's מצוה is broken by each night, so each day stands alone. The סוכה's מצוה goes on day and night, so the seven days are one long day and the wood stays holy for the whole חג.
